description: Test files that exist in this repository and are NOT executed by any hosted CI job. Every entry is a hole in the automated evidence, stated so that a reader of a green run knows what the green does not cover.
whyThisFileExists: apps/web/playwright.config.ts gates tests/e2e/authenticated/** behind ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH === '1', and no workflow sets it: .github/workflows/_reusable-node-quality.yml runs only `npm run test:web-e2e`, the anonymous tier. So the repository's ONLY tenant-isolation proof and its ONLY route-level accessibility proof had never once executed in CI, while `test:web-e2e` reported green and the phase records counted browser coverage. Nothing said so anywhere. This file, the LOUD job-summary step that reads it, and tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts are the replacement for that silence.
policy: An entry here is a debt, not a dispensation. It must name what is unproven in plain words, why a hosted runner cannot prove it, what compensates today, and a date by which the arrangement is revisited. tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts fails when a spec is neither executed nor declared, when a declared spec IS executed (a declaration must not be able to hide a runnable tier), when a field is missing, and when reviewBy has passed.
howToClose: Stand up Supabase and the API inside a hosted job, bootstrap an acceptance account, then run `npm run test:web-e2e-authenticated` with ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH=1 and delete the entry. Removing the entry without wiring the tier fails the gate, because the spec would then be neither executed nor declared.

unrun.whatItProves: That a signed-in operator of one tenant cannot see another tenant's records through the browser.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Tenant isolation is proved at the database layer by the RLS matrix and at the API layer by the backend suite. It is NOT proved end to end through a real session in a real browser, which is the only layer a customer experiences.
unrun.whyItCannotRunHosted: It needs a live Supabase GoTrue, a live API on port 3000 and a real account with a real password. The hosted clean room runs a bare postgres:17-alpine service container and sets NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY to a placeholder; there is no authentication server to sign in to.
unrun.compensatingControl: tests/db RLS matrix (critical level, run in both the clean room and database-security) and the backend authorization suite. The Owner acceptance run executes this spec by hand on a machine that has the full local stack.

unrun.whatItProves: Route-level accessibility of the signed-in application, against real rendered pages rather than components in isolation.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Component-level accessibility is covered by the web unit tier. Whole-page accessibility of authenticated routes — landmark structure, heading order, focus order across a real navigation — is proved by nothing that runs in CI.
unrun.whyItCannotRunHosted: Same three preconditions as E2E-AUTH-01: every authenticated route redirects to the login screen without a captured session.
unrun.compensatingControl: The anonymous browser tier covers the login, activation and gallery routes across five viewport and direction projects. The Owner acceptance run executes this spec by hand.

unrun.whatItProves: That the P1-27 CRM and Vehicle screens load and behave for a signed-in operator.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: The CRM and Vehicle screens are covered by the web component tier against mocked responses. No CI job drives them against a real API.
unrun.compensatingControl: The web component tier, the write-reachability gate (every canonical mutation has a real production call site) and the Owner acceptance run.

unrun.whatItProves: The administration screens for a signed-in operator, including at tablet width.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Administration screens are covered by the web component tier only.
unrun.compensatingControl: The web component tier and the Owner acceptance run.

unrun.whatItProves: The shared shell behaviour — scroll restoration, notifications, language switching — for a signed-in operator.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: The anonymous half of this behaviour IS covered, by tests/e2e/shared-ux-anonymous.spec.ts, which does run in CI. The signed-in half is not.
unrun.compensatingControl: tests/e2e/shared-ux-anonymous.spec.ts covers the same shell on anonymous routes in every hosted run.

unrun.whatItProves: The tablet drawer and scroll restoration on authenticated routes.
unrun.whatIsUnprovenWithoutIt: Drawer behaviour is covered by the web component tier; its behaviour inside a real authenticated navigation is not.
unrun.compensatingControl: The web component tier and the anonymous tablet project.
